findings.title: Optimized pagination branch uses a paginator that cannot handle datetime sort keys
findings.body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get passes order_by='-datetime' with OptimizedCursorPaginator. OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on the raw model field and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value, unlike DateTimePaginator which converts to/from timestamps. When any audit-log rows are returned, the key function receives a datetime and raises TypeError, and any non-empty cursor value would be compared as an integer to a datetime column. The optimized path is therefore broken and can return 500 or generate invalid queries.

findings.title: Negative offsets are passed to Django QuerySet slicing, which is unsupported
findings.body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset < 0, start_offset is set to the negative offset and queryset[start_offset:stop] is evaluated. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative start/stop values and raises AssertionError. Because cursor offsets are parsed from client-supplied strings, this allows a request to trigger a 500 instead of paginating.

findings.title: BasePaginator can pass negative previous-page offsets to QuerySet slicing
findings.body: The modified BasePaginator.get_result sets start_offset to cursor.offset whenever cursor.is_prev is true. Cursor.from_string accepts negative offsets, so a previous-page cursor such as 0:-1:1 causes queryset[-1:...] to be evaluated. Django does not support negative QuerySet indexing, so existing BasePaginator/DateTimePaginator endpoints can return 500 on malformed cursors.

findings.title: No tests cover the new optimized pagination mode
findings.body: The PR adds a query-parameter-controlled paginator switch, privileged access logic, negative-offset handling, and a new paginator, but no tests are included. Without tests for optimized_pagination=true, non-admin fallback, datetime cursor generation, and negative cursor offsets, these regressions are easy to miss.
